claims.label: The pilot wave
claims.summary: De Broglie presented a dynamics in which a real particle, with a definite position at every moment, is guided by a real wave; the particle's velocity is determined by the phase of the wave, and probabilities reflect ignorance of initial positions.
voice: I have tried to keep both pictures at once. The particle is real and has a definite position at every moment; the wave is real as well, and it guides the particle. The velocity of the particle is fixed by the phase of the wave. The probabilities then come from our ignorance of the initial positions, not from nature herself.
Why should we choose between the wave and the corpuscle, when the experiments show us both? Let the wave pilot the corpuscle.
claims.reasoning: Both diffraction patterns and localised detections are explained if a particle follows the wave's phase gradient.
claims.later: Abandoned by de Broglie within months; revived and completed by David Bohm in 1952; now known as de Broglie–Bohm theory.

claims.label: Matter waves confirmed
claims.summary: De Broglie's 1924 thesis proposed that every particle of momentum p has an associated wave of length h/p; electron diffraction in 1927 confirmed it.
voice: In my thesis I proposed that the association of waves with particles is universal: to every particle of momentum p there corresponds a wave of length h divided by p. This year Davisson and Germer, and Thomson, have diffracted electrons by crystals. The wave is not a metaphor.
claims.reasoning: Extension of Einstein's light-quantum duality to matter.

claims.label: The double solution — unfinished
claims.summary: De Broglie presented the pilot wave as a simplified version of his more ambitious 'double solution' theory, in which a singular wave represents the particle alongside the continuous wave; he acknowledged it was not complete.
voice: What I have presented is a simplified form. The fuller theory I call the double solution — a singular wave that is the particle itself, alongside the continuous wave we calculate. I have not completed it; the mathematics is hard, and I will not pretend otherwise.
claims.reasoning: The pilot wave is a provisional stand-in for a deeper theory.

claims.label: No full answer today
claims.summary: De Broglie did not answer Pauli's objection to his satisfaction at the council and abandoned the pilot wave soon afterwards. The wording of his reply here is inferred.
voice: Pauli's objection is serious, and I do not have a complete answer to it today. I believe it can be met, but I admit I cannot yet show how.
claims.reasoning: Honest uncertainty in the face of a pointed technical objection.
claims.later: He taught the standard interpretation from 1928 until 1952, when Bohm's work brought him back to causal interpretations.
